the activation of the CD4+CD25+, γδ+MCHII+ T cells and SIgm+ B cells in JD test positive cows was significantly higher than in JD test negative cows.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T and B cell populations in JD test negative animals respond to MAP stimulation in a similar manner, while JD test positive cows exhibit a more variable response.
the T and B cell responses in JD+ cattle are more robust and more variable than in JD- cattle.
JD+ cattle exhibit a greater diversity of activated T and B cells in response to MAP in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
JD test negative and JD test positive cows exhibit different immune responses against MAP.
JD test positive cows have an increased proportion of T cells expressing the activation marker CD25 after stimulation with MAP compared to JD test negative cows.
the immune response to MAP is complex and variable, and that the immune system of JD+ cattle may not always be able to mount an effective response against MAP.
